name: durable-spec-states-what-is
body:
A durable spec states what is. R1–R5 are the spec rules every APG instance applies to its durable tier 1–3 nodes, their notes, and their constraints. The rules govern the whole distributed agent suite APG ships — `opencode-suite/agents/*.md`, embedded into the `apg` binary via `include_str!` and installed by `apg init` into `~/.opencode/agents/`.

R1 — Positive definition. A tier-1–3 node states a positive, affirmative definition of what is, in the present tense. A node this change-set delivers reads as already true, because after merge it is. Negative rules and future-tense wording (will, shall become, planned, once X lands) belong in constraints, not tier nodes.

R2 — Negative rules live in constraints, scoped by layer. A constraint's layer is its scope: a `global.constraint.*` binds the whole durable spec for every APG instance, and a `<tier>.constraint.*` (requirements/domain/solution/implementation) binds that tier. A constraint declares its scope through its layer and names no single node — `attaches-to` is not part of the model (the law is `global.constraint.spec-constraint-scope`).

R3 — One note per node. A node has at most one note, and that note deepens the node's definition of what is.

R4 — A note details exactly one node. A note's `details` edge names exactly one node, never another note; the binary refuses a `Note`→`Note` `details` pair at write time.

R5 — No history. A spec node states timeless truth: the target reality, or what needs to become true. Git history describes the past; the durable spec describes what is. A spec node carries no change-log, no rejected alternative, no decision/reconciliation/correction/provenance record, and no time-relative wording that ages (today, now, currently, no longer, was, previously). A replaced statement is updated or removed, never annotated.

WRITER RULES — `spec-writer`, `plan-writer`, `codebase-navigator`:
- R1: author a positive, present-tense definition of what is; keep negatives and future tense out of a tier node.
- R2: place every negative rule in a constraint whose layer is its scope — global or a tier — and attach it to no node.
- R3/R4: give a node at most one note, deepening what is; a note details exactly one node and never another note.
- R5: author timeless truth; update or remove a replaced statement and leave no provenance trail.
- Run `apg spec lint` before hand-off and heed its warnings.

REVIEWER RULES — `spec-review`, `plan-review`, `implementation-phase-reviewer`:
- Run `apg spec lint` deterministically first and treat its errors as blocking.
- Judge every changed spec node semantically against R1–R5: positive/affirmative and present-tense (R1); negatives only in a layer-scoped constraint (R2); at most one note, deepening (R3); a note detailing exactly one non-note node (R4); no history content and no time-relative wording (R5).
- The fix is to DELETE or REWRITE the offending content to what is — never to add a note or annotate it.

ACCEPTANCE (prompt-only; assessed by review of the edited prompt files):
- `opencode-suite/agents/spec-writer.md`, `plan-writer.md`, and `codebase-navigator.md` state R1–R5 and the writer rules above.
- `opencode-suite/agents/spec-review.md`, `plan-review.md`, and `implementation-phase-reviewer.md` state the deterministic `apg spec lint` step and the semantic R1–R5 review, with delete/rewrite as the fix.
- The suite's `note` node type deepens the understanding of what is; no prompt instructs or expects a per-change provenance, decision, or reconciliation note.
